prompt.context: The client is the North American CEO of a global personal and home care products company. He has hired Capgemini Consulting to turn around the North American business from loss to profitability within two years. The project team is stranded at an airport and cannot make the final board presentation scheduled for this afternoon. You are asked to step in and make the presentation instead.
prompt.question: How would you structure the turnaround analysis, and what are your key findings and recommendations for returning the North American business to profitability within two years?

clarifying_info.q: What is the current financial situation of the North American business?
clarifying_info.a: The North American business is currently operating at a loss; the target is to return to profitability within two years.

clarifying_info.q: What product categories does the client operate in?
clarifying_info.a: The client is a global personal and home care products company with a large number of product categories.
Major competitors include P&G, Unilever, Johnson & Johnson, Avon, The Body Shop, Henkel KGaA, Reckitt-Benckiser, Shiseido, Jafra Cosmetics, Mary Kay, LVMH, L'Oreal, and Estee Lauder.
The North American business covering the USA, Canada, and Mexico.

exhibits.title: 2009-2014 Growth in Personal Care Consumption by Age Group (Male)
exhibits.shows: Bar chart of projected 2009-2014 growth rates in personal care consumption for male consumers, broken down by age group (0-24, 25-34, 35-54, 55+) and by country (Canada, USA, Mexico)

exhibits.title: 2009-2014 Growth in Personal Care Consumption by Age Group (Female)
exhibits.shows: Bar chart of projected 2009-2014 growth rates in personal care consumption for female consumers, broken down by age group (0-24, 25-34, 35-54, 55+) and by country (Canada, USA, Mexico)

exhibits.title: Ranking Major Household Spending Categories by Share of Wallet and Perception of Need
exhibits.shows: Scatter plot positioning household spending categories on two axes: Share of Wallet (Low to High, x-axis) and Perception of Need (Necessity to Luxury, y-axis). Personal Care and Household categories are among the items plotted alongside Insurance/Pension, Taxes, Housing, Food, Clothing, Recreation, Education, Donations, Tobacco/Alcohol, Household Furnishings, and Health Care.

exhibits.title: Product-Channel Strategy Map
exhibits.shows: Scatter plot mapping competitors on two axes: Number of Product Categories (0-16, x-axis, from Dedicated to Diverse) and Channel Strategy (y-axis, from Primarily Retail to Primarily Direct Selling). The client and named competitors are plotted. A trend arrow suggests movement toward more diverse product and channel strategies.

data.trend: Companies are moving toward more diverse product categories and more diverse channel strategies

framework: Customer Analysis: Identify consumer segments (age, gender, geography) and their relative sizes; assess how saturated key segments are; evaluate whether consumer tastes are shifting toward or away from client products
Internal Analysis — Revenue Streams: Examine existing and new product revenue; assess product portfolio breadth and positioning
Internal Analysis — Cost Drivers: Analyze R&D, manufacturing, and operations costs; identify duplicate costs and asset underutilization
Internal Analysis — Other: Supply chain design, channel strategy, financial situation, organizational structure, and core competencies
Industry Analysis — Competitors: Identify main competitors and the customer segments they target
Industry Analysis — Rivalry: Assess intensity of competition; look for consolidation trends, price wars, or segment-specific dynamics
Industry Analysis — Retailers: Map the retail channels used and assess retailer bargaining power

questions.prompt: Review Exhibits 1a and 1b. What are your observations about growth in personal care consumption across North America?
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies: (1) Women dominate consumption across all three regions and age groups — male growth rates are negligible by comparison. (2) Female Baby Boomers (55+ women) are the largest growth driver: 8.63% in Canada (35-54 bracket shown), 5.31% in USA (35-54), and 5.98% in Mexico (55+). (3) Generation Xers (25-34) are underrepresented in spending due to relatively small cohort size except in Mexico which had stronger population growth in that era. (4) Echo Boomers (0-24) will become more important post-2010 but are secondary in the short term. (5) Mexico shows stronger growth in the younger female cohorts relative to USA and Canada. Geographic nuances within North America must drive tailored marketing and product decisions.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 2. What does the Share of Wallet vs. Perception of Need data tell you about the opportunity for the client?
questions.guidance: A strong answer notes: (1) There is a direct co-relationship between perception of need and share of wallet — categories perceived as necessities capture larger wallet shares. (2) Personal Care represents only 1.7% of share of wallet in Canada, placing it in a relatively low-necessity, low-wallet-share position. Household Products capture 4.5%. (3) The strategic implication is that moving Personal Care products up the necessity axis (reframing them as essential rather than discretionary) is key to capturing a larger share of wallet. (4) Taxes, housing, and food dominate wallet share — the client is competing in a category that must win the perception battle to grow.

questions.prompt: Review Exhibit 3. What does the Product-Channel Strategy Map reveal about the client's position and the competitive landscape?
questions.guidance: A strong answer notes: (1) The client has a large number of product categories but appears to use a relatively dedicated/narrow channel strategy — this is misaligned. (2) The market trend shows companies moving toward more diverse channel strategies as product portfolios broaden, because different products require distinct channels and placements. (3) Companies with dedicated strategies (e.g., The Body Shop, Avon, Mary Kay) tend to rely on direct selling, which allows maximum consumer interaction. (4) Companies with diverse strategies (e.g., Estee Lauder) use multiple channels — prestigious retail, company salons, web. (5) The client should diversify its distribution channels to match its large product portfolio, or risk underserving certain product categories.

questions.prompt: Beyond the three exhibits, what additional considerations should the CEO be informed require further analysis?
questions.guidance: A strong answer organizes considerations into clear buckets. Key areas include: Make vs. Buy (in-house manufacturing vs. outsourcing — pros/cons, competitor benchmarks, key criteria); Customer perception (country of origin effects on brand and marketing strategy); Location/Distribution network design (does current network support future growth? what distance span optimizes service vs. cost?); Costs (differences between suppliers, standardized cost measurement across regions, consistency in accounting formulae, duplicate costs, asset underutilization, total delivered cost); Decision-making process (current vs. ideal Make/Buy process, accountability); Scalability (how distribution centers scale with growth projections, optimal number and range per DC); Information infrastructure (does the client have enterprise-wide visibility into inventory, costs, service levels? Is data comparable across regions and updated in real time?).

brainstorming.prompt: What additional considerations should be brought to the CEO's attention for further analysis to support the turnaround?

recommendation: The client should focus its consumer strategy on women — particularly female Baby Boomers — who represent the lion's share of consumption and growth, while monitoring the 55+ male segment and emerging Echo Boomer cohort. Marketing must account for geographic differences within North America.

The client should invest in understanding customer needs, perception, and spending patterns to reposition Personal Care products further up the necessity axis, enabling capture of a larger share of wallet — critical for sustainable long-term growth.

The client is misaligned on channel strategy: its broad product portfolio demands a more diverse, multi-channel distribution approach rather than a primarily dedicated strategy. It should investigate channel diversification with a rigorous cost-benefit analysis.
risks: The market may not continue growing at projected rates or may enter a period of decline
Threat of substitute products and shifting consumer trends could make personal care products less 'necessary,' compressing wallet share
Channel diversification involves execution complexity and upfront investment that must be managed carefully given the current loss position
next_steps: Segment-specific consumer research to identify unmet needs and willingness-to-pay across Baby Boomer, Gen X, and Echo Boomer cohorts in each country
Conduct channel strategy audit and build business case for diversifying distribution — including digital/e-commerce options
Standardize cost measurement across regions to enable meaningful comparison and identify quick-win cost reduction opportunities
Assess Make/Buy options for manufacturing with full total-delivered-cost framework
